why: THE FLIP WHITELIST: the backend symbols the boundary may still carry when --require-zero runs.
Every entry is a symbol that is PRESENT in the measured set TODAY, with the reason it is still
there and what removes it. The list may only SHRINK: an entry with no live hit is a failure
(the exception it claims no longer exists, so it must be deleted), and --update never touches this
file. A measured symbol that is not on this list fails the gate.
MEASURED TODAY (③-D/E item C, abi 16): 2 symbols. The third entry left in that batch - see
The engine's IMPORT reading is a separate instrument (every run prints it, --require-zero gates it)
and its number is not repeated here: it is whatever the gate prints.

departures.reason: vk_sampler::operator*() const. The engine used to READ the renderer's six samplers out of the backend's device root by dereferencing them; it now CREATES and OWNS them through the contract's create_sampler() (runtime::init_shared_samplers) and reaches the raw VkSampler through vulkan_escape::native_sampler(). An exit, not a silence: the symbol left the measured set.

entries.reason: initializer for module deren.vulkan.core. The engine imports a deren_vulkan module in ONE file now (the import instrument prints it: the legacy runtime's own declarations), and importing a backend module forces its initializer. It used to be three: vulkan/core/filter/filters.cppm stopped in the shared filter batch, and vulkan/readback/readback.cppm stopped in step 2's merged slice (it takes rhi::api_core& now). LEAVES WITH: the dynamic-link runtime, whose own declarations are the last importer - i.e. when the import check reads 0.

core::core(rhi::create_info const&). The engine still CONSTRUCTS the concrete backend class (runtime.constructor's std::make_shared<core>). LEAVES WITH: the dynamic-link runtime, which constructs through deren_make_api_core(rhi::abi_version, &options, &error_info) into a shared_ptr<rhi::api_core> and never names core.
